answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded random walks on an attestation graph, while each cut limits transition mass according to its conductance. An adversarial Sybil cluster resembles a glacier behind a sparse external cut: low conductance restricts legitimate signal entering it, and min-cut transitivity bounds cap its stationary aggregate voting weight. Even a coordinated whisper of cross-cut attestations cannot amplify that weight beyond the conductance bound.
